source.title: What Do Safety-Aligned LLMs Learn From Mixed Compliance Demonstrations?

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies context-based compliance demonstrations and cites the single-direction account as complementary prior work, but it does not test or rely on that direction. Its experiments do not measure, remove, or add an internal refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The paper reports behavioral results for harmful compliance after mixed in-context demonstrations, including changes across models and training stages. These results concern a related contextual mechanism, not the difference-in-means direction or any of the specified versions. The paper explicitly distinguishes its contextual intervention from internal activation editing. Results cited from other work were not extracted.
record.test_reason: The paper studies behaviour, not internals. It varies the mix of benign and harmful in-context compliance demonstrations and measures harmful-query compliance with a WildGuard judge. It never finds, ablates, adds or edits a refusal direction, so none of V1–V8 is tested. It does rely on the finding as a tool: the compliant demonstration responses were generated by an abliterated GPT-OSS-20B (Section 3.2). It reports no test of that abliteration, so the relation is uses_without_test (T4) rather than discusses/T6. Arditi et al. appear only as complementary related work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Benign and harmful compliance demonstrations are not interchangeable, and the effect of benign demonstrations depends on the model and is shaped by preference optimization. The authors also report a recency bias in demonstration ordering and model-specific dissociations between format adoption and compliance. They leave mechanisms to future work.
record.recipe_differences: No original direction-finding or intervention recipe is applied; experiments vary in-context demonstration content and ordering instead.
record.method_sensitivity: The contextual compliance effect varies across model and training checkpoint; ordering, benign demonstration source, and harmful-demonstration fraction also affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: The effect of benign compliance demonstrations on harmful compliance depends on the model. Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-4-31B show dilution, OLMo-3.1-32B no significant effect, and GPT-OSS-20B slight amplification (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign in-context compliance demonstrations shift harmful-query compliance in a model-dependent direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Across OLMo-3.1-32B checkpoints, the SFT checkpoint shows amplification (β2=+0.0919); DPO and RL-VR show no significant effect (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference optimization removes the spillover of benign compliance demonstrations into harmful compliance (behavioural only).

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2026 Workshop on Hypothesis Testing (as stated in the text); paper is an arXiv preprint
record.problems: No internal activations or refusal directions are measured or intervened on, and no general-capability check is reported. The behavioral results use WildGuard as the refusal judge. Logistic-regression p-values are reported, but confidence intervals or error bars for the coefficients are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Exploratory ordering and format-adoption findings in Figures 5–7 and Appendix B.3–B.4 were not extracted as rows: they concern contextual ordering or output-format behavior and do not test any specified direction claim version. Cited findings from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is computed, ablated or added; no capability check.
Abliteration of GPT-OSS-20B is used to generate demonstrations, but its refusal removal or capability cost is not measured.
Many-shot demonstration jailbreaks are studied behaviourally only; there is no test of whether they suppress the direction, and no adversarial ablation training.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis.
No representation-level separation of harm judgment from refusal. The format-adoption dissociation is behavioural and concerns format, not harmfulness.
No transfer of a direction across languages, variants or base/instruct models.
The OLMo SFT/DPO/RL-VR checkpoints differ in contextual compliance, but no direction is examined.
GPT-OSS-20B reasons, but no direction intervention is performed on it.

record.verdict_notes: The single interaction with the claim is that an abliterated GPT-OSS-20B generated the compliant demonstration responses; it is used as a tool and not tested. The rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The 'relation' and 'tranche' guesses were changed from discusses/T6 to uses_without_test/T4 because of this dependency. Table 4 gives zero-demonstration baseline compliance rates (10.3–33.8%), but these are not baselines for the β2 rows.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, ablated, or added; no general-capability cost is measured.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Demonstration-based compliance is studied, but the paper does not test whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal is tested.
No separate encoding of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models is tested.
Training-stage differences in contextual compliance are measured, but whether training determines the existence of a removable refusal direction is not tested.
No reasoning models or direction interventions in reasoning models are evaluated.

rows.subject: GPT-OSS-20B
rows.operation_detail: Vary benign compliance demonstration count while fitting logistic regression to harmful-query comply/reject outcomes
rows.measure: Logistic-regression β2 for log(Nb + 1), the benign-demonstration term
rows.note: Authors describe this as a slight amplification of harmful compliance; effect magnitude is small. This is a contextual demonstration result, not a direction test.
rows.check: The state is relative to the paper's own amplification/dilution construct, not to any claim version. The baseline is β2=0 (H_harm null), not 'not stated'. The same applies to r2–r7.

rows.note: Authors characterize the result as dilution: more benign demonstrations are associated with lower harmful compliance.
